questions.key_step: Product rule, then $\tan^{-1}x+\cot^{-1}x=\frac\pi2$.
questions.justification: One product-rule derivative with an obvious cancellation and one standard identity; no decision. (Question omits the factor $\frac1{2x}$ in the definition of $f$.) Same direct-evaluation demand as 2024-P2-Q1 (L0).

questions.key_step: Recognise a homogeneous curve as lines through the origin, so $y''=0$.
questions.justification: One familiar trick (homogeneous equation gives $y'=y/x$, $y''=0$) applied once; options help. Comparable single-move level to 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Compute $y'$ and $y''$ parametrically, then match powers of $t$.
questions.justification: Standard parametric second derivative followed by an exponent comparison; routine and short, with options. Level 1 on this scale since it is a single well-known formula.

questions.key_step: Even extension $f(|x|)$: extrema for $x>0$ mirrored, plus the corner extremum at $0$.
questions.justification: Needs a derivative of a rational function, its two real roots, and the symmetry/corner argument with a trap option 'None of these'; routine but multi-step. Easier than 2025-P2-Q8 (L4) which needs a non-routine analysis of $\frac{6x+\sin x}{2x+\sin x}$.

questions.key_step: Maximise $y^2$ after integrating; derivative factorises as $(1+t)(1-t)(\frac\pi2-1)$.
questions.justification: Two integrals, a sign argument for positivity, and a quotient-rule derivative with an algebraic factorisation that must come out right; two linked ideas but all standard. Similar chain to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2) plus an optimisation stage.

questions.key_step: Piecewise form of $f$ gives all of $I,M,N,C$ immediately.
questions.justification: Four quantities, each a one-line evaluation from the piecewise form of a sum of two modulus functions; no insight needed. JEE Main style.

questions.key_step: $g'=2f'(f+f'')=0$, so $g$ is constant.
questions.justification: One familiar recognition (factor $f+f''$) applied once; the question is a short, common pattern. Same single-move level as 2024-P2-Q10 (L1).

questions.key_step: Chain rule, noting the inner expression is $0$ at $x=1$.
questions.justification: Direct chain and product rule with one substitution; no insight. Lower than 2025-P2-Q14 (L3) where inverse-function derivatives are involved.

questions.key_step: Logarithmic differentiation at $x=0$ where $f(0)=1$.
questions.justification: Standard logarithmic differentiation done once, with easy arithmetic at $x=0$.

questions.key_step: Construct $f,g$ satisfying the hypotheses (double root at $1$) that falsify (A), (B), (C).
questions.justification: Needs a designed counterexample that meets three conditions at once, then three separate refutations; not a routine pattern but short once seen. Easier than 2026-P1-Q7 (L4) which has several counterexample-based statements.

questions.key_step: Spot that $1-5+4=0$ gives $\frac00$, then L'Hôpital (or linearisation) leaves $\frac{1}{9f'(0)}$, with $f'(0)=-\frac13$ read off the normal's slope.
questions.justification: Two familiar moves chained: normal slope to $f'(0)$, then L'Hôpital with chain rule on three composite terms; no real insight, single-correct with options. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Combine $\frac{f(x)}{x^2}\to\pi>1$ (so $f>0=f(0)$ near $0$) with the fact that a continuous, non-vanishing $f'$ keeps one sign on each side, to get a global strict minimum at $0$.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (limit gives local behaviour, non-vanishing continuous derivative propagates it globally) plus a counterexample to discard (C). The 'never vanishes means constant sign' argument is not a drilled pattern. Similar to 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Write cost as $kx+2k\sqrt{(20-x)^2+75}$ and solve $T'=0$, discarding the root outside $AP<AB$.
questions.justification: Standard optimisation word problem: set up, differentiate, solve one square-root equation. Several routine steps, no hidden idea; options available. Same demand as 2026-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Rewrite $\sin^{-1}\frac{2t}{1+t^2}$ piecewise ($2\tan^{-1}t$, $\pm\pi-2\tan^{-1}t$) so the sign of $f'$ flips when $|g|>1$.
questions.justification: A very standard identity with three branches, then three one-line monotonicity checks; the trap is statement (iii), where two reversals give increasing. Routine chain, single-correct with options. Near 2021-P1-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Solve the two curves simultaneously to get the double root $x=1$ (or use the reflection symmetry in $y=x$), then read off the common tangent $y=x$ and normal $x+y=2$ at $(1,1)$.
questions.justification: Routine chain: eliminate, factor $(x-1)^2(x^2+1)$, find slopes, write tangent and normal; each statement is a quick check, all within tangents and normals. Like 2024-P2-Q7 (L2).

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=\cos x$ and find the minimum of $t^t$ at $t=\frac1e$ via $\phi'=t^t(\ln t+1)$; then notice $t^t\to1$ at both ends so $\ln2$ is not attained.
questions.justification: Standard $t^t$ minimum plus careful statement checks (open range, not attained supremum, closed interval in (D)) in a one-or-more-correct question. A notch above routine because of the half-open range trap. Compare 2026-P2-Q8 (L2) and 2025-P2-Q8 (L4).

questions.key_step: Read $f''>0$ as 'slope strictly increasing' for (A), (B), and for (C) see that a convex function with $f'(0)>0$ grows at least linearly so cannot have a finite limit.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a genuine check; (A), (B) are quick but (C) needs the convexity-plus-limit argument and (D) an example. One-or-more-correct, single concept. Similar to 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Two real roots of $f'$ means discriminant $>0$, and $3\lambda^2+8\lambda+12$ is always positive, so the condition holds for all real $\lambda$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (discriminant of $f'$); the only care is to see that the condition holds for every real $\lambda$, so all four sub-intervals are correct. Similar to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1).

questions.key_step: Eliminate $y=k-x$ and factor $f'=x^{m-1}(k-x)^{n-1}[mk-(m+n)x]$ (or use weighted AM-GM), giving $x=\frac{mk}{m+n}$ and the value $\frac{m^mn^nk^{m+n}}{(m+n)^{m+n}}$.
questions.justification: Routine symbolic optimisation with a known shape; a few steps and a careful look at the options (C and D are the same expression, B is false unless $m=n$). Easier than Advanced. Close to 2026-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Find $f(0)=2$ so $g(2)=0$, then use $g'=\frac{1}{f'}$ and $g''=-\frac{f''}{(f')^3}$ at $x=0$.
questions.justification: Two standard inverse-derivative formulas chained with a small evaluation; second-derivative formula is a bit less drilled but options guide the student. Easier than 2025-P2-Q14 (L3, numerical).

questions.key_step: Split $\frac{1}{x^2-1}$ into partial fractions to get the $n$th derivative, and use that differentiation flips parity.
questions.justification: Routine chain: a standard partial-fraction nth derivative plus a parity argument, four statements each checked quickly; two concepts (nth derivative and even/odd) so the multi-correct floor 2.5 applies. Same demand as 2023-P2-Q1 (routine chain, L2).

questions.key_step: Chain rule: the sign of $f'$ times the sign of the inner derivative decides each composite.
questions.justification: Four one-line chain-rule checks with a single idea (sign of a composite derivative); no casework. Similar to 2024-P2-Q10 (L1, monotonicity from the sign of a derivative).

questions.key_step: Since $g(\pm1)=0$, failure of Rolle's theorem forces a zero of $f$ inside $(-1,1)$; then test the remaining statements with counterexamples.
questions.justification: Statements phrased as 'which is false' need the decoding of why Rolle's theorem fails and then counterexamples for C and D, with negative-marking risk. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q7 (L3, implications with counterexamples).

questions.key_step: Apply LMVT to $f^n$ to get $f'(c)f(c)^{n-1}=\frac{2^n-1}{n}$, then AM-GM with strict inequality.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (LMVT on a power of $f$, then AM-GM on a GP with a strict-inequality check) and the 'not guaranteed' options need a counterexample. Familiar trick for $g=f^n$, so not Level 4. Near 2021-P2-Q3 (L2) in chapter but longer and with an inequality stage.

questions.key_step: Odd degree of $p'$ gives a root; Rolle's theorem between roots gives at least $2020$; build counterexamples ($x^2\prod(x-k)$, $x^4$) for C and D.
questions.justification: Four conceptual statements on polynomials (IVT on odd degree, Rolle counting, extrema test) where the false ones need constructed counterexamples; no heavy computation. Same kind of demand as 2026-P1-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Model the cost as $x+2\sqrt{25+(\ell-x)^2}$, differentiate and keep the root inside $[0,\ell]$.
questions.justification: Standard single-variable cost minimisation: set up the model, one derivative, one squaring step (extraneous root) and substitution; options present. Routine chain, no insight needed. Easier than 2026-P2-Q3-type chains of equal length only in modelling; placed at L2.

questions.key_step: The cost is convex, so on $[0,10]$ the maximum is at an endpoint; compare $f(0)=10\sqrt5$ with $f(10)=20$.
questions.justification: One recognised idea (maximum of a convex function at an endpoint) plus two evaluations, in the same set-up as the previous question. Routine, Level 2 rather than 1 because the convexity argument must be supplied and the options include the minimum point as a trap.

questions.key_step: Trace the graph from the sign data and count roots of $f(x)=|x|$ and $f(x)+3x=0$ piece by piece using monotonicity, convexity and end limits.
questions.justification: Long chain with high precision risk: the graph must be reconstructed from derivative signs, asymptotes and concavity, then roots counted in five regions using convexity and the given inequalities; one missed region changes the count. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q14 (L4, counting with several regions); paragraph parts rate high on this scale.

questions.key_step: $f(-|x|)$ mirrors the $x\le0$ part of the graph: corner at $x=\pm2$ and one-sided derivatives $\mp f'(0)$ at $0$.
questions.justification: Needs the idea that $f(-|x|)$ uses only the left half of the graph and so inherits the corner at $-2$ at two points, plus the one-sided derivative check at 0; short but not in a standard drill. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q7 (L3, continuity/differentiability implications).

questions.key_step: Evenness gives zeros $\pm\alpha,\pm\beta,0$ of $f'$ (from the zigzag of values), and Rolle's theorem on $f'$ forces four points of inflection.
questions.justification: Non-routine idea: turning a zigzag of four values and evenness into five zeros of $f'$ and then into a minimum count of inflection points; numerical answer with no options and a sign-change subtlety. Idea availability places it above routine L3 items such as 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Space diagonal = diameter gives $a^2+b^2=6$; AM-GM gives $ab\le3$.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (diagonal relation, volume expression, AM-GM) with no real insight; numerical format and no options to check, so a little above a single-trick question. Comparable in demand to 2021-P2-Q18 (L2).

questions.key_step: Reciprocal-polynomial substitution $g=x+\frac{1}{x}$ with $|g|\ge2$, then maximise $\frac{(g+2)^2}{g^2-g-1}$.
questions.justification: The substitution is not obvious (palindromic structure in numerator and denominator), then a maximisation on a restricted range $|g|\ge2$ where the branch $g\le-2$ must be dismissed; numerical answer, no options.

questions.key_step: Critical points $0,1,2$ with $f=-1,1,-1$ give four sign changes, so four real roots.
questions.justification: Routine chain (derivative, factor, three values, sign argument) with a standard idea; numerical, but short and no pitfalls. Similar demand to 2021-P1-Q17 (L1) with a longer chain.

questions.key_step: Symmetry gives seven zeros of $f'$; spot that the expression is $(f'f'')'$, count $13$ zeros of $f'f''$ and apply Rolle.
questions.justification: Long chain of distinct stages (symmetry gives extra zeros, Rolle twice, recognising $(f'f'')'$) with counting precision and no options; the idea of recognising $(f'f'')'$ is non-routine. Close to 2021-P2-Q9 (L4).

questions.key_step: Substitute $x^{1/3}=2-g$ to recover $f(x)=x^3-7x^2+11x+2$, then locate the local maximum.
questions.justification: Routine chain: invert the cube root, expand, differentiate, second-derivative test; only mild idea (recover $f$ from the composition). Slightly easier than 2025-P2-Q14 (L3).

questions.key_step: Increasing $f(f(x))$ versus decreasing $\frac{4}{x^2-4x+6}$, with the solution $x=2$ found by inspection.
questions.justification: Standard monotonic-intersection argument for an unknown increasing $f$; the domain remark and spotting $x=2$ are the only subtleties, and the answer is a single digit. Compare 2024-P2-Q10 (L1), slightly longer here.

questions.key_step: Chord relation $x^2=2R^2(1-\cos\theta)$ and $\dot\theta=\frac{v}{R}$, differentiated at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
questions.justification: Standard related-rates problem: set up the chord, differentiate, substitute; several routine steps and no real insight. Level-2 'routine multi-step' as in 2026-P2-Q2.

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=x-\frac{1}{x}$ to get $y=\frac{1}{t^2+2/t+3}$, then AM-GM; the system part is routine.
questions.justification: Two separate routine parts joined by $k$: a substitution plus AM-GM maximisation (needs the identity $x^3-\frac{1}{x^3}=t^3+3t$ and split AM-GM) and a $3\times3$ system. More stages than 2021-P1-Q12 (L2) and 2021-P1-Q7 (L1), so level 3.

questions.chapter: Inverse Trigonometric Functions / Function / Definite Integration
questions.key_step: Principal values give $k=6$; the functional equation yields $f'(x)=f'(0)+2x^2$; odd symmetry finishes the integral.
questions.justification: Three short stages from three chapters (ITF branch care, functional equation to derivative, integral with symmetry); each is standard coaching material. Similar to 2024-P2-Q8 (L2) in the functional-equation part, longer chain, so level 3.

questions.key_step: Compare $f(0)=\sin1+1$ with $f(0^+)=\sin\lambda+1$ (after checking the left side is increasing) to get $\sin\lambda\le\sin1$.
questions.justification: Piecewise junction analysis with a small trap (equality at $\lambda=1$, and $\lambda=2$ just outside $[\pi-1,2\pi]$), then integer counting; answer is a digit, no options. Close to 2025-P2-Q8 (L4) in topic but much shorter, so 3.

questions.key_step: Model the smallest enclosing rectangle as $(a+b)b$ and see that the answer is the maximum, not the minimum, over all pairs of squares.
questions.justification: The modelling is the hard part (disjoint projections, 'least A for every pair' means a max over pairs, and $a<b$ constraint), followed by a routine calculus maximisation; answer is not unique unless in lowest terms. Similar to 2021-P2-Q7 (L4) where geometric modelling sets the level.

questions.key_step: Solve $x^4-13x^2+36\le0$ to get $|x|\in[2,3]$ and see that $f$ is monotonic there, so ignore $x=\pm1$.
questions.justification: Routine chain: factorise a biquadratic inequality, differentiate, notice the critical points are outside the domain, evaluate endpoints. The only trap is using $x=\pm1$; the odd-symmetry shortcut makes it even lighter. Same demand as 2021-P1-Q12 (L2).

questions.key_step: Find $x_0=1$ with $f(x_0)=-\frac76$, use $g'=1/f'(x_0)$, then differentiate $h$ term by term.
questions.justification: Three short stages (inverse derivative, spotting $x=1$, fractional-power derivative and ratio) with no options to check; the inverse-derivative idea is standard. Close to 2025-P2-Q14 (L3) in demand.

questions.key_step: Differentiate $g(f(x))=x$ three times (or reverse the series) to get $g'''(0)$ from $f',f'',f'''$ at $0$.
questions.justification: Needs the repeated inverse-function differentiation (quotient rule applied twice), a less drilled idea than the first derivative of an inverse, but the arithmetic is tiny and the pattern is familiar to prepared students. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q14 (L3).

questions.key_step: Interlacing from $f'g\ne g'f$ (Rolle on $f/g$), then Rolle twice more, recognising $(g')^2+gg''=(gg')'$.
questions.justification: Existence/Rolle counting with a hidden structure: students must see the interlacing consequence of $f'g\ne g'f$ and the product-derivative form. Three stages, but each is a standard Rolle application; no heavy calculation. Placed at average Advanced (L3), comparable to 2023-P2-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Create two equal values by IVT, then Rolle (or use an interior maximum).
questions.justification: A proof with one idea chain: IVT to manufacture equal values, then Rolle; the method is standard for prepared students, but it is a proof rather than a calculation. Equivalent to 2021-P2-Q3 (L2) in demand (IVT/Rolle).

questions.key_step: Reading asymptotes and sign changes of a rational function; part (d) needs the argument that concavity must change twice.
questions.justification: Parts (a)-(c) are routine reading of a rational function's graph; part (d) needs the less drilled idea that a positive function vanishing at both ends forces concave-down stretches, with a parity split. Multi-part with mixed demands, average Advanced; comparable to 2025-P2-Q8 (L4) for the curve-analysis flavour but lighter.

questions.key_step: Case analysis on $a$ for the position of the minimum and the larger end value; the tight bound $\frac32-\sqrt2$ vs $\frac1{12}$.
questions.justification: Proof-style with a parameter: convexity, three cases and two sub-cases, and a tight numerical comparison ($289>288$) where a slip breaks the argument; no options to check. The slick three-point argument exists but is not the usual route. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q8 (L4) for casework-heavy extrema.

questions.key_step: Express $V$ in terms of the level $h$ ($a=h+2$) and apply $V'=(h+2)^2h'$ at $h=1$.
questions.justification: Routine related-rates chain: similar triangles for the side, frustum volume, differentiate, evaluate; no insight beyond standard setups. Equivalent to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2) in routine multi-step demand.

questions.key_step: Model $f=x\sqrt{1-x^2}$, $g=xf$, then four routine optimisations/integral.
questions.justification: Four short calculus items on one model; each is routine (derivative, factorise, integral) and options allow elimination, though item (c) needs a careful derivative and factorisation. Lighter than 2026-P1-Q16 (L3) which mixes conics; matching average is about 2.

questions.key_step: Find $f=x^4-2x^2+4$ from the conditions, then factorise four expressions.
questions.justification: Determining the quartic is routine, and the four equations factor in one or two lines each ($4x^3-3x-1=(x-1)(2x+1)^2$ is the only slightly hidden one); options allow elimination. Same demand as 2024-P1-Q14 (L2).
